subject: Chemistry
q: Which titration arrangement determines the concentration of an aqueous NaOH solution most accurately, assuming a suitable indicator is used?
options: NaOH solution in a volumetric flask and concentrated H₂SO₄ in a conical flask
NaOH solution in a burette and concentrated H₂SO₄ in a conical flask
NaOH solution in a burette and standard aqueous oxalic acid in a conical flask
NaOH solution measured with a pipette and aqueous oxalic acid in a burette
hint: Use a stable primary standard and place the solution being standardized in the burette.
solution: NaOH is hygroscopic and absorbs CO₂, so it is a secondary standard whose concentration must be established against a primary standard. Oxalic acid can be prepared at an accurately known concentration, unlike concentrated H₂SO₄. A measured aliquot of standard oxalic acid is placed in the conical flask and titrated with the NaOH solution from the burette. Therefore the third arrangement is the most accurate.
